goal: Serialize durable campaign lessons and share their retained provenance across worktrees
asset: Existing LessonV1 append-only memory and recorded run artifacts
scope: Cross-process lesson append locking and newest-by-time serving
Clone-shared git-common-dir storage with explicit override and legacy adoption
Retained shared run copies for lesson provenance
Evidence recording survives malformed lesson stores
outOfScope: Repairing malformed historical JSONL by guessing missing bytes
Recall index writer serialization handled in separate change

record.question: Where should parallel worktrees retain lessons safely?

options.strongest_objection: Needs compatible legacy reads and serialized append transactions
Removing a worktree deletes its lessons and siblings cannot seed them

record.rationale: Use the existing cross-platform workfile lock and git common directory so worktrees share durable local knowledge.
evidence: Issues #160 and #165 include measured concurrent tearing and deletion repros
Existing workfile_lock handles POSIX flock and Windows msvcrt

costs.cost: One filesystem lock per append and one shared run copy
evidence: Existing cross-platform lock and immutable run artifacts are reusable

requirements.statement: Concurrent appends preserve complete rows and cumulative arrivals; linked worktrees share surviving lessons and retained provenance; legacy adoption preserves original files
requirements.counterexample: Two simultaneous writers tear a row or count a third arrival as two, or deleting the filing worktree loses its lesson

requirements.statement: A malformed lesson store remains a hard error to memory readers but cannot suppress a run Evidence row
requirements.counterexample: SystemExit during lesson filing terminates record-run before Evidence is appended

checks.scope: Execute multiprocessing writers, linked worktree deletion/adoption and record-run with corrupt memory
assumptions: Filesystem advisory locks are honored by cooperating memory writers
No remote host synchronization is claimed

challenges.claim: Does a shared store imply cross-host synchronization?
challenges.resolution: No. FPL_MEMORY_HOME selects an explicitly synchronized location; synchronization remains external.

challenges.claim: Should corrupt JSONL be silently skipped?
challenges.resolution: No. Readers still refuse corruption; record-run isolates that failure so Evidence survives.
